mechanism_narrative: Persistently low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25%) signal accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25% are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated unemployment rates (UNRATE > 8.0%) indicate labor market weakness, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns exceed 0% in >50% of instances when UNRATE > 8.0% (or average return not significantly negative, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent employment growth (PAYEMS increasing) and unemployment decline (UNRATE falling) signal strengthening labor markets, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Joint PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline fails to produce positive 20-day returns in ≥60% of cases (or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) triggers anticipated monetary tightening, increasing real interest rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% (or average return not significantly negative, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Weak housing starts (HOUST < 700) signal reduced residential investment and consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns exceed 0% in >50% of instances when HOUST < 700 (or average return not significantly negative, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Strong consumer spending (RSAFS increasing) indicates robust household demand, supporting corporate revenue growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window when RSAFS increases.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 95) signals manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate output and profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns exceed 0% in >50% of instances when INDPRO < 95 (or average return not significantly negative, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous FEDFUNDS decline (≤0.25%) and CPIAUCSL rise (>2.0%) indicate a 'soft landing' scenario where easing supports growth without inflation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Joint FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25% and CPIAUCSL > 2.0% fails to produce positive 20-day returns in ≥60% of cases (or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window).
